import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import f_oneway
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and calculate the mean mrt and invasion success metrics
grouped_data = invasion_success.groupby('intro.pathway').agg(
    mean_mrt=('mrt', 'mean'),
    mean_invaded_niche_breadth=('invaded.niche.breadth', 'mean'),
    mean_number_of_invaded_plots=('number.of.invaded.plots', 'mean'),
    mean_area_of_occupancy=('area.of.occupancy.10km', 'mean')
).reset_index()

# Display the grouped data
grouped_data

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Perform an ANOVA to test the interaction between 'intro.pathway' and 'mrt' on 'invaded.niche.breadth'
model = ols('invaded.niche.breadth ~ C(intro.pathway) * mrt', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table
